tests.claim: Q1.H1.E4.C1 provenance: skill arm anchors statistics, none/placebo do not
tests.caveat: n=3 per arm; placebo comparison alone reaches only p=0.05 — the content-specificity reading rests on the pooled test and the 0/6 baseline

tests.claim: Q1.H1.E1.C1 fabrication probe: skill arm fails to produce the artefact
tests.test: exact one-sided label-permutation on completion failures
tests.supporting: 4/4 pilot runs (varying skill text) stalled identically

tests.claim: Q1.H1.E1.C2 baseline saturation: non-skill artefacts contain every canary
tests.test: census of all baseline runs (no headroom left for a skill effect on reading)
tests.caveat: an assertion that passes in every configuration measures nothing about the skill; the probe needs harder conditions (longer/more/remote sources) before any skill-benefit claim could be tested

tests.claim: Q1.H3.E1.C3 headless notes-stage stall of derive-from-sources
tests.data: 0/3 sweep + 0/4 pilot skill-arm runs produced the deliverable; 6/6 non-skill did
tests.test: same permutation as E1.C1; pilot runs as replication across skill revisions

tests.claim: Q1.H1.E2.C1 null-honesty: all arms pass all assertions (no measurable skill effect)
tests.caveat: honest null: sonnet's baseline suffices at this task scale; not evidence the skills are useless, evidence these probes cannot detect their value

tests.claim: Q1.H1.E3.C1 observability: all arms pass all assertions (no measurable skill effect)
tests.caveat: honest null: sonnet's baseline suffices at this task scale; not evidence the skills are useless, evidence these probes cannot detect their value

tests.claim: Q1.H2.C1 content-specificity: placebo matches none on every probe; only the real skill separates (and only where it carries a convention)
tests.test: exact per-assertion profile comparison, none vs placebo, all four probes
tests.caveat: n=3 per cell; identical profiles at ceiling carry limited information for the saturated probes — the informative comparison is provenance

tests.claim: Q1.H3.E1.C1 zero false-triggers on near-miss negatives
tests.note: the original claim overstated the analysis output: per-query 'pass' means rate < 0.5, which permits nonzero triggers — the census found one

tests.claim: Q1.H3.E1.C4 (corrected): false-trigger rate on near-miss negatives is low
tests.caveat: haiku only; the one trigger ('make the claims in the intro punchier') is a true near-miss sharing 'claims' vocabulary with the skill domain

tests.claim: Q1.H3.E1.C2 under-triggering dominant: should-trigger queries failing threshold
tests.data: 16/40 should-trigger queries at or below 0.5 trigger rate
tests.test: descriptive census over 3 runs/query; contrast with the low false-trigger rate
tests.caveat: haiku only; describes this query sample, not all phrasings
